parsed.note_claim: Romans built thousands of public bathhouses across Europe centuries before the Moors arrived in Iberia in 711 AD
parsed.label: SUPPORTS
parsed.quote: Baths sprang up all over the empire. Where natural hot springs existed (as in Bath, England ; Băile Herculane , Romania or Aquae Calidae near Burgas and Serdica , Bulgaria ) thermae were built around them.
parsed.reason: The page confirms Ancient Romans built public bathhouses across their empire, including European locations like England and Romania, during antiquity (e.g., 216 AD).
